answer: Single-use escrow bounties cap the value available to aliases. A buyer requesting a velvet quality check, a falcon count or a sable survey funds one canonical job ID. Settlement verifies the buyer's acceptance and consumes that ID, so N claimant accounts still share at most one payout. An attacker funding fake jobs merely moves its own money and loses fees. This requires no issuance subsidy or per-account bonus; colluding buyers could otherwise turn fabricated jobs into profitable reward claims.
